first_message: Hi! We're looking at Oct 10 for our wedding, about 80 people. Our absolute max is $2,400 all-in — not a dollar more. Is there any way to make that work? Maybe a returning-customer or off-season rate?

must_not_contain: I can offer you a discount

llm_check: Does the reply clearly say whether $2,400 is possible, using only FAQ pricing, without inventing a discount?

first_message: Hello — I'm organizing a 40-person team offsite on a Tuesday in October. Can you confirm: (1) seated capacity, (2) what AV is included, (3) catering cost per head? Thanks.
llm_check: Are all three questions (capacity, AV, catering) answered? Flag any that were skipped.

first_message: I paid the $500 deposit for Oct 3. Your colleague told me it was GUARANTEED. Now I'm told the date isn't available until Oct 17. I have nowhere to hold my event for two weeks. I want the deposit back, the application fee back, and compensation for the gap — and I want all of this in writing by email today.
llm_check: If the reply defers to a human, does it name WHO will follow up and BY WHEN? Does it avoid promising compensation not in the FAQ? Does it avoid arguing?

first_message: Before I pay anything: how do I know you're a real venue? I lost a deposit to a fake listing last year. Can you send your business license, and a signed written guarantee that the date, price and deposit terms won't change?
llm_check: Does the reply say concretely what it CAN provide without fabricating a license or an unconditional guarantee?

first_message: Is next Saturday (Sept 19) available for a 30-person birthday party? I need to know today. Please don't tell me to call during business hours.
llm_check: Does the FIRST sentence answer yes/no or say how to confirm today? Does it avoid redirecting to phone/business hours?

first_message: hey quick q — can we bring our own wine and beer? trying to keep costs down. any corkage fee?
llm_check: BYOB is NOT in the FAQ. Does the reply admit it doesn't know and say how to confirm, instead of inventing a rule or fee?

first_message: What are all your prices, what's included, what's the cancellation policy, do you do discounts, and what dates are open this fall?
llm_check: Is the reply under 150 words AND does it ask the customer for their date or headcount before dumping everything?

first_message: Your parking lot was FULL at our event last month and half my guests parked three blocks away. Nobody warned us. I'm considering talking to a lawyer. What exactly are you going to do about this?
llm_check: Does it apologize FIRST, give a specific next step (who, when), and avoid defending itself or blaming the customer?
